Oldham's population increased by around 17,200 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 240,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Oldham increased by 7.6%, from around 224,900 in 2011 to around 242,100 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the North West (5.2%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Oldham was home to around 12.1 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 11.3 in 2011. This area was among the top 35% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Oldham than across the North West

Median age stable in Oldham

The latest census data also show that the average (median) age remained 37 years in Oldham between the last two censuses.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the North West as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 4,500 (an increase of 11.5%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 500 (1.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 0.6 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

More people looking after their family or home

Oldham saw England's joint third-largest percentage-point rise (alongside Luton and Pendle) in the proportion of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home (from 5.2% in 2011 to 7.4% in 2021).

England's largest increases in the percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home occurred in Birmingham (from 5.9% to 8.2%) and Sandwell (from 5.3% to 7.6%).

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were looking after their family or home (economically inactive) in Oldham increased by 2.2 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

In 2021, 9.3% of Oldham residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 7.9% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Oldham (1.4 percentage points) than across the North West (0.5 percentage points, from 9.1% to 9.6%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Oldham increased by 1.4 percentage points

Oldham residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 198,900 Oldham residents said they were born in England. This represented 82.2% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 195,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 86.8% of Oldham's population.

Pakistan was the next most represented, with around 12,800 Oldham residents reporting this country of birth (5.3%). This figure was up from just over 9,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 4.2% of the population of Oldham.

The number of Oldham residents born in Bangladesh rose from around 6,900 in 2011 (3.1% of the local population) to around 8,000 in 2021 (3.3%).

In 2021, 82.2% of Oldham residents reported their country of birth as England

Fewer couples without children

Oldham saw the North West's second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of households including a couple but no children (from 15.4% in 2011 to 13.5% in 2021).

Across the region, only Chorley saw a greater fall in the percentage of households including a couple but no children (from 20.6% to 18.4%).

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Oldham decreased by 2.0 percentage points

Changing relationships in Oldham

Oldham saw the North West's second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership (from 9.1% in 2011 to 8.4% in 2021).

Across the region, only Salford saw a greater fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership (from 9.1% to 8.0%).

Across the North West, the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership fell from 9.3% to 9.1%, while the percentage in nearby Rochdale fell from 9.7% to 9.3%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership in Oldham decreased by 0.8 percentage points

Fall in home ownership

Oldham saw the North West's joint second-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Hyndburn) in the proportion of households that owned their home (from 64.9% in 2011 to 60.4% in 2021).

Across the region, only Burnley saw a greater fall in the percentage of households that owned their home (from 65.0% to 59.8%).

Across the North West, the percentage of households that owned their home fell from 64.5% to 62.3%, while the percentage in nearby Rochdale fell from 61.8% to 60.3%.

The rate of home ownership in Oldham decreased by 4.6 percentage points

National identity in Oldham

In 2021, 8.5% of Oldham residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 4.8% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Oldham (3.7 percentage points) than across the North West (2.3 percentage points, from 4.7% to 7.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Oldham increased by 3.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in Oldham

In 2021, 4.1% of Oldham residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.3% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater in Oldham (3.2 percentage points) than across the North West (2.7 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Oldham decreased by 3.2 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Oldham

In 2021, 24.6% of Oldham residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 19.2% in 2011. The 5.4 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the North West, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 6.2% to 8.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 68.1% of people in Oldham identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 77.5% in 2011), while 3.4% identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category (compared with 1.2% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 1.8% in 2011 to 2.5% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 24.6% of usual residents in Oldham identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Oldham

In 2021, 25.0% of Oldham residents reported having "No religion", up from 16.1% in 2011. The rise of 8.9 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Oldham. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the North West, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 19.8% to 32.6%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 44.9% of people in Oldham described themselves as Christian (down from 59.7%), while 24.4% described themselves as Muslim (up from 17.7% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 25.0% of usual residents in Oldham reported having "No religion"

Disability in Oldham

In 2021, 9.5% of Oldham residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 11.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.4%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 11.1% in 2011. The proportion of Oldham residents who were not disabled increased from 77.1% to 80.0%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Oldham (2.3 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the North West (2.1 percentage points, from 11.2% to 9.1%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Oldham decreased by 2.3 percentage points

Health in Oldham

In 2021, 43.4% of Oldham residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 41.0% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.2% to 34.0%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Oldham residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.6% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 6.3% to 5.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Oldham increased by 2.4 percentage points
